timestamp.description:
The timestamp when the feedback was provided.

This field stores the exact date and time the user submitted their feedback in `datetime` format.
It represents the time when the feedback was created.

createdByUser.description: The information of the {@link User} that created it.

id.description:
A unique identifier that can be manually assigned or generated automatically during object creation. This
identifier cannot be altered after the object has been persisted.

version.description:
Version number used for optimistic concurrency.  Automatically managed by the system.

Updating an Obj with a null or 0 value for version will cause the concurrency check to be skipped and should only
be done with great caution.

typeWithBindings.description: Persists concrete type with bindings for generic types where instance has parameter bindings

typeIdent.description:
Indicates explicit sub-type of entry.  Composed of the concatenation of the typeKey of the instance's type and all
of its base type's typeIdent

alert.description:
The {@link ReliabilityAssetAlert} this feedback is for.

This field stores the reference to the alert that the user is providing feedback about.
The `ReliabilityAssetAlert` represents a system-generated alert, and this feedback helps assess whether the
alert was useful or a 'false positive.'

The `alert` field is a required field and must be set to the relevant alert for the feedback.

category.description:
The category of feedback that the user selected.

This field specifies the feedback category that the user has selected from a predefined list. This categorization
allows for structured feedback, helping to identify trends or common issues across multiple alerts.

The `category` is a string field, and the values are enumerated by the {@link ReliabilityAssetAlertFeedbackCategory} enum,
which defines various types of feedback such as 'False Positive', 'Useful', 'Requires More Data', etc.

comment.description:
The provided user feedback.

This is the actual textual comment or feedback provided by the user. It is typically a free-form field where users
can describe their experience or opinion on the alert, such as why they think the alert was or wasn't useful.

This field helps provide qualitative context to the feedback, making it possible to understand the user's reasoning
behind the chosen feedback category.

title:
Registers provided by the {@link User} on an alert, giving feedback about how functional the system-generated
{@link ReliabilityAssetAlert}s are. This process prevents the occurrence of 'false positives,' ensuring the system's
accuracy and reliability and ultimately improving the user experience to make it better and more efficient.

**Purpose:**
- This entity stores user feedback on the reliability alerts generated by the system.
- The feedback helps in assessing and refining the quality of the alert system, especially in terms of reducing false positives.
- The system uses this feedback to improve its accuracy and reliability over time.
- The entity helps link the feedback to the relevant alert and maintains detailed user information for tracking purposes.
name: ReliabilityAssetAlertFeedback
